2024 Personal project

Prison Break — Escape Big Sister

No engine. Everything from scratch, in Python.

  • RoleGame Designer · Developer
  • TeamSolo
  • TimelinePersonal project
  • StatusReleased — source public
  • Built withPython · Pygame
Play in browser on itch.io Source on GitHub Read the source

The project

A 2D stealth and parkour game: break out of a prison of cold, unfeeling machines without being caught in Big Sister's line of sight. Built in Pygame, which means there was no engine doing any of the work — collision, input handling, state management, the camera, rendering and the game loop are all code I wrote.

What I owned

  • Collision detection and resolution
  • Input handling and character state machine
  • Stealth and detection logic
  • Rendering and the main game loop
  • Design and level layout

A problem I solved

Pygame gives you a window, a blit call and an event queue. Everything a commercial engine hands you for free — the collision system, the camera, the animation state machine, the scene structure — either gets written by you or does not exist.

That is the entire reason this project is on my portfolio rather than a Unity version of the same idea. Working without an engine is what turned "Unity does this" into "this is how this works, and here is why it is done that way." It made me a considerably better Unity developer.

Result

A finished, playable stealth game, and the source is public — so if you want to know how I actually write code rather than take my word for it, this is the one to read.
